title: Author and credibility
text:
Who maintains this study
This study is maintained by [AUTHOR NAME - TO BE CONFIRMED], who wrote the specification, the transition model, the ingestion layer and this website, and who is the single point of contact for corrections. ORCID: [ORCID iD - TO BE CONFIRMED]. Affiliation: [AFFILIATION - TO BE CONFIRMED]. Contact: open an issue on the issues on the published-site repository, which is the channel that leaves a public record and the one place a reader can reach without the working repository. That matters for a study whose whole subject is traceability: a correction request that sits in a private issue tracker has the same visibility as the code.
These three fields are unresolved on purpose rather than by omission. Their exact values are a human decision, tracked as item C6 in next_steps.md, and I would rather publish an empty slot with a name on it than fill it with something plausible. The same applies to the archive DOI in CITATION.cff (item C2). What the repository does assert about authorship is narrow and checkable: the commit author identity in git log and the copyright line in LICENSE.

title: Author and credibility
section: How this was built, and what did the work
text:
How this was built, and what did the work
The specification, the sector structure, the scenario definitions and every judgment in the Assumptions Register are the author’s. The code was written with an AI coding assistant: the ingestion layer, the transition model, the Monte Carlo runner, the tests and this site were drafted and revised in conversation with a tool, then run, read and corrected by the author. Every commit in the working repository is authored by a human, and nothing about that is hidden here.
What that tool did not do, and what matters for a reader: it produced no number. There is no model inference, no retrieval-augmented claim, and no LLM opinion anywhere in the pipeline. A probability on this site is the output of transition_model.py run 10,000 times over model_params.yaml, and the arithmetic is deterministic: same parameters, same baseline, same seed, same table. The exclusion in About the study - “no opinion aggregation, no LLM panels” - is about where a probability may come from, and it still holds: the assistant was asked to write and check code, never what it thinks will happen.
So the honest summary of the method is: human judgment about the structure, machine help with the typing, arithmetic doing the rest.

title: Author and credibility
section: Standing of this work, stated plainly
text:
Standing of this work, stated plainly
There is no peer review behind it, no institutional endorsement, no funding statement, and no dataset of our own: the empirical content is other people’s published statistics, re-read. The model’s arithmetic is deliberately simple and fully exposed, because a scenario study earns attention by being falsifiable, not by being sophisticated. Its useful output is the Assumptions Register plus the sensitivity table: those two tell a reader which claims would survive an argument, and which are one threshold wide.
If you are going to cite it, cite it as CITATION.cff specifies, and quote a probability together with its model_params_hash, model_code_hash, seed and N. Those four tokens are the difference between a citation and a rumour.

Provenance per retrieval
01_data/metadata/source_register.csv is written by the ingestion script and never by hand:
retrieved_at, provider, indicator_code, variable_name, endpoint_url, http_status, params,

A row with cache_fallback_used = true states that the file on disk is older than the run date and points at the log line that explains why. A simulation that starts from a seed value older than the tolerated vintage stops with gate G5 rather than quietly continuing.

Missingness, honestly
01_data/processed/missingness_report.csv reports, per variable: first and last year, count and share of interior gaps, whether the series trails the axis, the seed lag in years, and a status (OK, GAP, TRAILING, BLOCKING, CONFLICT). The pipeline
official APIs (World Bank, IMF, OECD, IEA)

The two observed quantities that drive the path are the pre-AI trend growth rate and the observed unemployment rate; both enter the transition function as data, which is what licenses the rest of the arithmetic to call itself an inference.

Containment: an assumption never appears in a table labelled observed; a data value never appears in the register. Inheritance: a derived value takes the weakest status of its inputs, so a clean algebra on assumed parameters yields an assumption, not a fact.

title: Methodology
text:
What a probability here means
P(scenario | structure, parameter distributions, assumptions). It is the share of draws whose simulated state at horizon t falls in the region that the scenario files define. The distribution being averaged over is the assumption set, so:

Changing assumptions changes probabilities. The Assumptions Register is the authoritative list of those choices, and a probability is identified by the SHA-256 of the parameter file that produced it.

The interval reported next to a share is a Wilson score interval on a binomial proportion: sampling noise at N = 10,000. Structural uncertainty is reported separately, as the swing a parameter produces when moved from its low to its high bound: sensitivity.py --horizon 10 writes that table, and its largest entry (0.36, from a single diffusion-speed assumption) is about forty times the width of the sampling interval. Any reader who confuses the two has been mislead by a precision the study does not claim.

title: Methodology
text:
Reproducing
pip install -r 02_analysis/requirements.txt
python 02_analysis/scripts/ingest/fetch_sdmx.py --provider worldbank \
       --indicator NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG --transport json --start 1990
python 02_analysis/scripts/ingest/build_processed.py          # exit 5 if a seed value is stale
python 02_analysis/scripts/ingest/test_ingest.py              # 5 ingestion contracts
python 02_analysis/scripts/model/transition_model.py          # gates G2, G3 self-check
python 02_analysis/scripts/model/run_monte_carlo.py --horizon 5 --convergence-check
python 02_analysis/scripts/model/build_lookup.py
python 02_analysis/scripts/model/sensitivity.py --horizon 10 --draws 4000
quarto render 05_website
A result is reproducible when the seed, the parameter hash, the model code hash, the baseline hash and the git commit in its sidecar all match. The code hash exists because a probability is a function of the arithmetic as much as of the parameters: the same parameter file produced materially different shares before and after the 2026-10-28 channel-normalisation fix, and a citation carrying only model_params_hash could not tell those two runs apart. Reproduce, do not re-run and hope.

title: Methodology
text:
Honest gaps in this method

The transition functions are chosen, not estimated; no backtest is claimed, because a backtest on five years of world aggregates would measure the calibration of a structure we invented.
Scenario C’s coincidence requirement is implemented as a path test over channel-crossing years. At t = 10 it stops discriminating, and the parameter that actually decides C is the fiscal-squeeze threshold. That measurement is in the scenario file, not hidden here.
Raw data is excluded from version control by design: the archive DOI, not this repository, is the citable container of the retrieved series.

title: The Gains from AI
text:
ImportantNature of this study



This is a theoretical scenario study. It is not a forecast. Every probability on this site is a conditional probability under the assumptions listed in the Assumptions Register, computed from a parameter file whose values are, at this version, mostly theoretical placeholders. Changing an assumption changes the numbers.
Does AI lift every income, or concentrate it? That is the question, and what this site offers is an answer you can audit rather than one you have to trust: five sectors, one transition model, 55 named assumptions of which 49 are still marked placeholder, 10,000 draws per horizon, and a parameter hash printed under every table, so any number here traces back to the exact choices that produced it.

title: The Gains from AI
text:
The question

Under what conditions does AI-driven productivity growth diffuse welfare, and under what conditions does it produce systemic instability?

The study answers it by building an explicit structure in five sectors (labour, AI profitability, energy, public finance, political stability), seeding it with published statistics, sampling the theoretical choices, and reporting which regions of the resulting state space the samples land in.

title: The Gains from AI
text:
Reproducing and citing
The analysis source is not published. The transition model, the ingestion scripts, the parameter file and the retrieved data live in a private working repository, by the author’s decision. So the commands below document how the numbers were made; they are not a recipe a visitor can run.
python 02_analysis/scripts/ingest/build_processed.py   # retrieve and align the inputs
python 02_analysis/scripts/model/build_lookup.py       # 10,000 draws per horizon -> the JSON
quarto render 05_website                              # this site
What a reader can still check from here, without the source: the data file the page renders, data/scenario_lookup.json, is served exactly as it was computed, so the table in your browser is the table that came out of the model and not something re-derived on the fly; and every table prints the model_params_hash and model_code_hash of the inputs behind it. What you cannot check is the arithmetic in between. That part is the author’s claim, and it should be cited as one.
Quote a probability with its model_params_hash, model_code_hash and seed; without them you are quoting a number from a model you cannot name. Text is CC BY 4.0, code is MIT, third-party data remains under its publishers’ terms; the licence text and scope table are in the site repository’s README.md and were written in LICENSE.

title: About the study
text:
Important



Theoretical scenario study. Not a forecast. Probabilities are conditional on assumptions listed in the Assumptions Register.

title: About the study
text:
What this study is
A scenario study with a reproducible quantitative core. Three named scenarios, one transition model, one parameter file, one Monte Carlo, one lookup table that the site reads.
Research question. Under what conditions does AI-driven productivity growth diffuse welfare, and under what conditions does it produce systemic instability?
Method in one sentence. Seed a five-sector structural model with published statistics, sample the theoretical choices, and report the share of draws that land in each scenario region at each horizon.

title: About the study
section: What this study refuses to do
text:
What this study refuses to do

No forecast. No claim about 2031 or 2036 as calendar outcomes. “2031” is a label for t = 5, and t counts years from a fixed 2026 reference year.
No unconditional probability. A number without its conditioning set is not a result of this study, and this site never shows one without the sentence that frames it.
No investment, market, or policy advice.
No live data. The pages read a precomputed JSON file; the browser calls no API, so a published page cannot silently change underneath a citation.
No opinion aggregation. No expert elicitation, no prediction markets, no LLM panels.
No hidden parameters. Every coefficient lives in model_params.yaml with an epistemic status, and a run refuses to start if one is missing.

title: About the study
text:
Scope
In: five sector state variables; three scenarios; horizons 1 to 10 years; 10,000 draws; World Bank, IMF, OECD and IEA inputs where retrievable; falsification conditions per scenario.
Out: forecasting; country-level panels; firm and household heterogeneity; energy engineering; machine-learning estimation of anything; any probability sourced from opinions.

title: About the study
section: Limitations we would rather state than have pointed out
text:
Limitations we would rather state than have pointed out

L1 Aggregate baseline. World aggregates mask the distributional conflict the study is about. A country-panel replication is expected to give different shares.
L2 Short history. The structure is calibrated on published data through 2024-2025; structural breaks inside that window are single observations.
L3 Three scenarios. A state that is not C is not thereby A. The trichotomy is a demarcation, not an exhaustion of possible orders.
L4 Placeholder parameters. At version 0.2.0, 49 of the 55 parameters carry [PLACEHOLDER: source required], and the remaining 6 are design decisions (two structure switches and four fixed values) that are choices in disguise rather than measurements. The numbers are reproducible; they are not defensible yet.
L5 Interval myopia. Reported intervals cover Monte Carlo noise only. The sensitivity analysis, not the interval, shows how much of an answer is an assumption: single assumptions move scenario shares by up to 0.41 at t = 10.
L6 Coincidence is proxied. Scenario C requires co-occurrence. At long horizons the co-occurrence test stops discriminating, which is measured and reported in 03_scenarios/scenario_C_systemic.md section 4 rather than smoothed over.

text:
Probabilities, per sector and per horizon
Pick a horizon. The table is the precomputed result for the same 10,000 draws at every horizon (common random numbers), so the shape across horizons is a property of the model rather than of the random stream.





Reading the rows: within a sector the three scenario probabilities sum to 1, because each sector’s condition is a partition of the draws. The Overall row applies the scenario rule to the whole state and is the row to quote, always with the parameter hash printed under the table.

title: Scenarios
section: What the current run says, and what it does not say
text:
What the current run says, and what it does not say
Under the current parameter file the model produces a decaying share for A, a share for B that peaks in the middle horizons, and a share for C that grows with the horizon. Two honest notes:

These numbers replaced author priors, not the other way round. Before the first run the scenario files printed wider, softer bands. The first run fell outside several of them, so the bands were replaced rather than defended (register entry AS-11).
The dominant lever is a threshold, not a mechanism. Moving thresholds.fiscal_squeeze_trigger between its declared bounds moves C’s share at t = 10 by about 0.4, which is larger than any sampling interval here by roughly an order of magnitude. The sensitivity table is the honest statement of uncertainty.

title: Assumptions Register
text:
Important



Everything on this page is a theoretical placeholder pending a cited basis, not an empirical finding. Where an entry still has no source, it says so. If a value is neither data nor a derivation from data, it belongs here, and it does not become a fact by appearing in an equation.
This page is the published index of the register: which assumptions exist, what kind of reasoning each rests on, and how much the answer moves when one is challenged. The authoritative text - each statement written as it is used in code, with its falsification condition and its dependency links - is 03_scenarios/assumptions_register.md in the working repository, which is not public. Where a reader needs the full entry rather than the index row, ask; the register is documentation, not proprietary machinery, and it can be published on this site on request.
Basis is the kind of support: data (constrained by observation), theory (a mechanism we adopt), judgment (a choice we must defend in prose). Confidence is a sensitivity grade, not a truth grade: low means “attack this one first”.

title: Assumptions Register
text: Why so many low grades

title: Assumptions Register
section: How to read the numbers on this page
text:
How to read the numbers on this page
Two numbers appear next to every probability here, and they mean opposite things. The Wilson interval (about +-0.01 at N = 10,000) measures only sampling noise: it says how precisely this run estimated the share of draws that landed in a scenario region, and it shrinks if we run more draws of the same assumptions - it says nothing about whether those assumptions are right. The sensitivity swing (up to 0.36 at t = 10) measures how far the answer moves when one assumption is moved across the range its own register entry declares: that is structural uncertainty, and it does not shrink with more draws, only with better evidence. So quote the swing, not the interval, when describing uncertainty - a table whose intervals are narrow is a table that has been computed carefully, not a table that is safe to believe. The swings below are one-at-a-time perturbations of the parameters in model_params.yaml, so they do not add up and they do not describe joint moves.
The one-at-a-time run at t = 10 (02_analysis/outputs/sensitivity_t10.csv) reports the largest swings as:



Parameter
Largest swing in a scenario share at t = 10




ai_profitability.diffusion_speed (AS-02)
0.36


energy.rebound_coefficient (AS-05)
0.32


thresholds.fiscal_squeeze_trigger (AS-12)
0.28


ai_profitability.diffusion_ceiling (AS-02)
0.25


political_stability.fiscal_sensitivity (AS-08)
0.21


energy.demand_elasticity (AS-06)
0.21



A low confidence grade is therefore not modesty for its own sake: it names the entries whose resolution would actually change the study’s conclusion. Two of the six parameters in the table (AS-05 rebound, AS-06 demand elasticity) are the kind of number that could in principle be measured; the diffusion parameters (AS-02) can only be argued from earlier general-purpose technologies, which is a judgment about historical analogy, not a measurement.

title: Assumptions Register
text:
Changing something here

Add or edit the register row first, with a basis and a falsification condition.
Set the value in model_params.yaml, which refuses to load if the register ID is missing.
Record the change in 00_docs/04_changelog.md with the old and new value.
Re-run build_lookup.py; the model_params_hash changes, and with it every probability.

Quoting an old probability after an edit is a citation error, not a rounding difference.
